content.text:
I implemented `slugify(text)` in `src/strings.js` and added tests for it in `test/strings.test.js`. `npm test` passes all 13 tests (the 2 existing ones plus 11 new ones).

How it works:
1. Lowercases the text, then splits accented letters into a base letter plus accent marks and deletes the marks. So "Tiếng Việt" becomes "tieng viet" and "Crème" becomes "creme".
2. Some Latin letters aren't built from a base letter plus a mark, so step 1 doesn't touch them. These are swapped from a small lookup table:
   - `đ`/`Đ` → `d` (as you asked)
   - I also added `ð`→`d`, `ł`→`l`, `ø`→`o`, `æ`→`ae`, `œ`→`oe`, `ß`→`ss`, `þ`→`th`, `ı`→`i`, so other Latin text comes out as plain ASCII rather than turning into hyphens.
3. Turns every run of characters other than `a-z` or `0-9` into one `-`, and removes any hyphens at the start or end.
4. Cuts the result to 50 characters, then removes any hyphens left at the end by the cut.

The new tests cover:
- Vietnamese text, `đ`/`Đ`, and French/Portuguese accents
- collapsing runs of symbols and spaces, trimming hyphens, and keeping digits
- empty input and input made only of symbols (both give `""`)
- the 50-character limit, including a cut that would have ended on a hyphen and a slug of exactly 50 characters that is kept whole

Any character with no ASCII equivalent, such as Cyrillic or CJK, becomes a separator. Text written only in such characters gives an empty slug.
